findings.problem: Requiring the constant coefficient to lie in V unnecessarily excludes polynomials with an arbitrary constant offset, although differentiation ignores that coefficient.
findings.proposed_change:
With the existing ambient variables, generalise the statement to:
 theorem directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule (V : Submodule ℚ L)
     (h : σ → ℚ) (P : VectorPolynomial σ ℚ L)
     (hP : ∀ α, α ≠ 0 → coefficients P α ∈ V) :
     ∀ α, coefficients (directionalDerivative h P) α ∈ V
The existing sum-and-scalar-closure proof still works: apply hP to α + Finsupp.single i 1, which is nonzero because its value at i is α i + 1. Existing callers supply the weaker hypothesis directly from their current coefficient assumptions.
findings.benefit: Supports differentiation of V-valued polynomials plus constants outside V, including nonzero constants when V = ⊥. Empty σ and zero directions remain valid: the derivative is zero.

findings.problem: The conclusion only concerns membership in V ⊔ F.layer j, but the coefficient assumptions exclude components in F.layer j outside V. Those components can be allowed because the enlarged submodule is already invariant under U.
findings.proposed_change:
Keep the existing ambient variables and generalise the statement to:
 theorem polynomial_removal_preserves_derivative_layers
     (U : LieSubalgebra ℚ L) (V : Submodule ℚ L)
     (hUV : ∀ u ∈ U, ∀ v ∈ V, ⁅u, v⁆ ∈ V) (j : ℕ)
     (A C : PolynomialGroup σ F.lowerCentralSeries_eq_bot)
     (hAU : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ U) (hCU : ∀ α, coefficients C.coord α ∈ U)
     (hAV : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ V ⊔ F.layer j)
     (hCV : ∀ α, coefficients C.coord α ∈ V ⊔ F.layer j)
     (t h : σ → ℚ) (small rational : L)
     (hsmall : small ∈ V ⊔ F.layer j) (hrational : rational ∈ V ⊔ F.layer j) :
     dualAdjoint (polynomialValueHom t A)⁻¹ (small - polynomialLogDerivative t h A)
         ∈ V ⊔ F.layer j ∧
       dualAdjoint (polynomialValueHom t C) rational - polynomialLogDerivative t h C
         ∈ V ⊔ F.layer j
For the proof, set W := V ⊔ F.layer j. Obtain its invariance from F.invariant_sup_layer U V hUV j, establish the tangent memberships in W with the existing coefficient argument, and invoke F.derivative_removal_preserves_quotient_layers with W instead of V. Simplify W ⊔ F.layer j to W by sup_assoc and sup_idem.
findings.benefit: Allows removal polynomials whose coefficients are controlled only modulo the relevant filtration layer, including nonzero layer-valued coefficients when V = ⊥. No positivity assumptions are needed: for j ≤ 1 the target is ⊤, and for j ≥ s + 1 the change reduces to the original assumptions.
